title: Watch must treat gRPC Unavailable on Send as consumer disconnect, not an error
answers: Watch stream logs errors when the client disconnects
how to handle srv.Send failing because consumer is unavailable
spurious errors in Watch when gRPC transport closes
Unavailable error sending events to Watch consumer
body:
Symptom: Watch() returned/logged an error whenever srv.Send failed because the consumer disconnected or its backend became unavailable (observed as transport-level codes.Unavailable).
Root cause: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go Watch() propagated raw srv.Send() errors (bookmark send, catch-up iterator send, live event send) up the call chain.
Fix pattern: wrap every srv.Send error with watchSendError(err) (server.go), which detects status.Code(err)==codes.Unavailable and wraps it in sentinel errWatchSendUnavailable; the deferred cleanup in Watch() converts that sentinel to a nil return, matching the existing clean-shutdown handling for context cancellation.
Constraints: only gRPC Unavailable is treated as clean shutdown; other codes and context errors from unrelated contexts must still propagate. Apply watchSendError() at every new srv.Send call site added to Watch().
applies: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go Watch() and any new srv.Send call sites added there
